If your goal is to lose weight, I don't recommend starting with strength training. I recommend starting with cardio. Easy way to lose weight? Jog 15 km every two days like I do. I lost 23 kilos two summers ago just by doing that.

Eat balanced and make sure you get enough protein (should be easy - no need to waste money on supplements), carbohydrates, healthy fats, fibre, and enough calories to grow on. If you're obese and really want to drop fat insanely fast go very very low carb, like an almost no carb paleo type of diet for a while (don't do it for too long) and it will give you a quick boost in fat loss.

For training find something you can do everyday for GPP (General Physical Preparedness). In the gym (or your own home gym) focus all your energy and attention on these basic movements:

Squat

Press (standing overhead press)

Deadlift

Bench press (or push ups or dips)

Pull ups or chin ups

Maybe also throw in some kind of row too (barbell rows, dumbell rows or inverted rows).

And work your neck too (either with a harness or with manual resistance)

If you don't have any money to buy equipment or a gym membership then just train using your own bodyweight and whatever you can find at home.

Do bodyweight squats instead of barbell squats and work up to where you can load up a backpack full of sand, books, bottles of water, rocks or whatever you have.

Do handstand push ups against a wall instead of the barbell press and work up to where you can do it with both of your hands on some stacks of books or bricks or something so you can go all the way down and work up to doing them away form a wall so you're also working on balance.

Find something heavy you can lift from the ground instead of doing the barbell deadlift such as rocks, buckets full of sand or water (or wet sand!), random hunks of metal, anvils, engine blocks, a military duffel bag full of sand, logs, whatever.

Instead of the bench press do push ups or dips on parallel bars (or between two chairs) and again work up to added resistance with a backpack or someone lying on your back etc.

Same thing with the pull ups or chin ups. Find a place to do them (park, door way pull up bar, a tree, whatever) and work up to adding resistance with a backpack or chains or whatever.
